readme.html:
Agentic Awesome Skills — AI Skills & AAS Core

Find reusable instructions for your project, inspect their complete files, and keep an exact skill set you can review and reuse.

Agentic Awesome Skills is a library of 2,957+ installable SKILL.md playbooks for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI and other AI coding agents. AAS Core helps Codex or Claude search the complete local catalog, record the skills the agent chooses, and preview a plan you can inspect before changing a target. Core does not rank or recommend skills.

Start here: Explore the skill catalog · Codex setup · Claude Code setup · Install or update without npm

[!IMPORTANT] npm publishing paused. Publishing new AAS versions to npm is paused while the maintainer account is locked. Use GitHub for current skills and updates. Installation and update guide.

Project identity: Agentic Awesome Skills (AAS) was previously named Antigravity Awesome Skills. The official repository is sickn33/agentic-awesome-skills, and the official website is aaskills.tech. Original code and tooling use MIT; original written content uses CC BY 4.0. Imported skills retain their own license and attribution requirements; see License.

Current release: V20.8.0. AAS Core supports local catalog inspection, agent-owned selection, stack validation, and plan preview. Apply and recovery remain experimental. Read the AAS Core preview guide for setup and exact trust boundaries.

This README tracks main. Features listed under Unreleased require a later release; the versioned guide describes the published package.

This is an independent community project, not affiliated with or endorsed by Google. Google, Antigravity, Gemini, and related names describe compatibility and install targets. The GitHub repository is canonical; the hosted catalog and browser-local Workbench are companion discovery and review surfaces.

For a complete setup through your first skill selection and installation preview, follow Codex setup or Claude Code setup.

AAS Core: Agent-First Preview

Codex or Claude inspects your project and chooses exact skills. Every current catalog skill is individually searchable, readable, and available for agent selection. The read-only compose_stack tool validates the chosen IDs and structure in memory; a client or the aas CLI can persist aas-stack.json and optional selection evidence. aas stack validate checks the manifest, while aas stack plan writes an immutable preview for your review. Manifests have a technical maximum of 128 skills; Core does not rank or recommend candidates or install skills in this supported preview path.

[!IMPORTANT] Structural and identity validity does not certify semantic fit, compatibility, setup correctness, operational safety, or safety to apply. Apply and recovery require experimental opt-in and remain outside the supported preview.

The Workbench reviews stack and plan artifacts in browser memory without accessing your filesystem. See the Core guide for tool contracts, capability coverage, and limits.

Installation

From selection to use

With AAS Core already configured, use the Core guide to review the exact skill IDs your agent selects. The npm-based bootstrap for the current Core release is paused. You can install the skills themselves directly from GitHub.

Install selected skills directly

With GitHub CLI and gh skill available, preview and install one skill from the current release. This example uses Codex at user scope:

gh skill preview sickn33/agentic-awesome-skills skills/brainstorming/SKILL.md@v20.8.0
gh skill install sickn33/agentic-awesome-skills skills/brainstorming/SKILL.md --agent codex --scope user --pin v20.8.0

To update a pinned skill, preview it at the newer release tag and repeat the install with that tag. See the installation and update guide for other agents, switching from an npm install, downloading a ZIP, and updating a Git clone.

Bundles & Workflows

Bundles suggest related skills; workflows describe the order to use them. They are guidance for selecting and running skills, not additional packages to install.

  • Bundles group skills by role or goal, such as Web Wizard, Security Engineer, and OSS Maintainer.
  • Workflows give ordered playbooks for planning, shipping, testing, and auditing; workflow metadata is available for integrations.
  • If too many installed skills overload Antigravity, follow the selective activation guide. For other hosts, preview a smaller exact install or use the installer's --risk, --category, and --tags filters.

Browse 2,957+ Skills

Explore the complete library in the hosted catalog or CATALOG.md. The canonical playbooks live in skills/; skills_index.json provides machine-readable discovery. Use Getting Started and Usage for first steps, or the Workbench to inspect a saved Core stack and plan in your browser.

For narrower comparisons, see Claude Code skills, Cursor skills, and the library comparison.

Host integrations that load individual SKILL.md files can use skills_index.json, the v1 schema, and the compatibility mirror. This direct-host discovery manifest is separate from aas-stack.json and the AAS Core catalog. Read the discovery contract before integrating.

Contributing

  • Add new skills under skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.md and follow CONTRIBUTING.md.
  • Start from the skill template and run npm run validate before a PR.
  • Keep source PRs free of generated registry artifacts. Skill content and risky guidance require manual logic and safety review alongside automated checks.

Community

  • Discussions for questions, ideas, and examples.
  • Issues for reproducible bugs and actionable improvements.
  • Follow @AASkills_ on X for project updates and examples, or @sickn33 for releases.
  • CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md for community expectations; SECURITY.md for security reports.

skills.name: accesslint-audit
skills.description: Find and fix WCAG 2.2 accessibility issues. Two modes — report (sweep a codebase or page, produce a prioritized written report, no edits) and fix (audit→edit→verify loop on a target). Prefers direct-CDP live-DOM auditing; falls back to a browser-MCP composition or HTML-string audits.

skills.name: accesslint-diff
skills.description: Diff a live page's accessibility violations against a baseline — by default compares uncommitted changes (stash-based), or pass --branch [name] to diff against a branch. Reports only new violations introduced, violations fixed, and pre-existing count. Use `scan` for a full audit with no diffing.

skills.name: accesslint-scan
skills.description: Audit a live page for accessibility issues, locate each WCAG violation precisely, and return a selector-grounded fix worklist without editing.

skills.name: fixing-accessibility
skills.description: Audit and fix HTML accessibility issues including ARIA labels, keyboard navigation, focus management, color contrast, and form errors. Use when adding interactive controls, forms, dialogs, or reviewing WCAG compliance.
